description: 2 tactical challenges for Black in the Winawer Poisoned Pawn. Meet 7.Qg4 with accurate defense and generate counterplay against White's exposed queen.

drills.briefExplanation: 6...Ne7 unpins, then meet 7.Qg4 with 7...Qc7 8...Rg8 — and strike back with 9...cxd4.
drills.description: Black to play. White's center is imposing after 6.bxc3 — find the unpinning 6...Ne7 and the plan against 7.Qg4.
drills.explanation: 6...Ne7 is the only move that keeps Black's position together, breaking the pin on the f6 square. After 7.Qg4 Qc7 Black defends g7 indirectly; 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7 looks terrifying, but 9...cxd4 opens the position while White's queen is stranded on h7. Follow up with ...Nbc6 and ...Bd7, and Black has real compensation in activity.
drills.name: Sidestep and Counter

drills.briefExplanation: 8...Rg8 9.Qxh7 cxd4 — the rook comes alive and the center opens while White's queen is offside.
drills.description: Black to play. White has just grabbed on g7 — activate the rook and blast the center open.
drills.explanation: 8...Rg8 is the key defensive resource: the rook both attacks the queen and prepares to dominate the g-file. After 9.Qxh7 cxd4 Black's idea is clear — open lines before White consolidates. 10...Nbc6 develops with tempo on d4, and 11...Bd7 prepares ...O-O-O, when the half-open g-file and central pressure give full compensation for the pawns.
drills.name: Holding the Counterplay

name: Winawer Poisoned Pawn — Black Tactics
